name: Lu'an Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Lu'an Economic Development Zone Administrative Committee / China Mobile Lu'an Branch / Dongfang Supercomputing (Lu'an) Technology
notes: Official Lu'an sources say the center's planned investment is RMB 240 million for 1000 PFLOPS; phase 1 was completed and put into operation in June 2024, with later official response reporting 400 PFLOPS delivered and a 1200-rack A-grade Lu'an cloud-computing data center in use.

name: Guodong Big Data Industrial Park
developer: Guodong / project sponsor not fully specified in planning text
notes: Lu'an digital creative industry planning consultation lists a Jin'an District project with about RMB 8 billion total investment, 213 mu site, 200,000 sqm floor area, intended to introduce 5G smart manufacturing and build a high-grade large cloud-computing and big-data industrial center serving East China.

name: E-Link Matrix Intelligent Computing Center
developer: China Unicom / Lenovo Group / Huashan District partners
notes: Government repost says Huashan District is building vertical-industry AI model training compute capacity and investing RMB 500 million with China Unicom and Lenovo in the E-Link Matrix intelligent computing center, planned for about 2500 PFLOPS.

name: Anhui XiangYun Cloud Data Centre
developer: Anhui XiangYun Cloud / project team not fully specified
notes: Weak primary-person account describes a retrofit cloud data-centre project in Ma'anshan that began in July 2015 and was completed in November 2015; included for coverage but should be independently verified.

name: Suzhou Computing Power Industrial Park Data Centers
developer: Suzhou High-tech Zone / local compute-industry operators
notes: Xinhua/Anhui Daily reports Suzhou has planned a RMB 5 billion, 230,000 sqm computing-power industrial park with five data-center buildings totaling 100,000 sqm; two buildings totaling 40,000 sqm are operational with more than 5000 racks.

name: Huaihai Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Huaihai Intelligent Computing Center / Suzhou compute-industry partners
notes: Xinhua/Anhui Daily describes the Huaihai center in Suzhou High-tech Zone as delivering about 300 PFLOPS of intelligent computing, supporting government services, enterprise R&D, model training, and Yangtze River Delta digital transformation.

name: VNET Anhui (Suzhou) Data Center
developer: VNET Group, Inc.
notes: DataCenterMap lists VNET Anhui (Suzhou) at No. 1790, Bianyang 3rd Road, Suzhou, China. Public listing confirms operator and location but not capacity.

name: Tongling Intelligent Computing Center
developer: China Telecom Tongling Branch
notes: Tongling Natural Resources and Planning Bureau reports the project has broken ground in Tongling Economic and Technological Development Zone and is planned as intelligent compute infrastructure with 2500 IDC racks, serving government cloud, industry cloud, and enterprise AIDC workloads.

name: Huawei Cloud East China (Wuhu) Data Center
developer: Huawei Cloud
notes: Huawei says the Wuhu data center formally opened in June 2024, covers about 6000 mu across Jiangbei, Sanshan, and Vocational Education Park zones, and is planned for 3 million servers with liquid-cooling/AI cluster architecture.

name: China Telecom Wuhu Cluster Big Data Center and Yangtze River Delta (Wuhu) Intelligent Computing Center
developer: China Telecom Anhui / China Railway Construction East China Engineering
notes: Wuhu public-source report and China Telecom say construction started July 25, 2024; when complete it will provide more than 80,000 standard racks and become China Telecom's largest Yangtze River Delta data center.

name: Wuhu National Data Center Cluster Start-up Area
developer: Anhui Provincial Government / Wuhu municipal authorities / multiple operators
notes: Anhui government measures define the Wuhu cluster start-up area as Jiujiang District, Yijiang District, and Wuwei City. Trade reporting says Huawei Cloud, China Telecom, China Mobile, China Unicom, Sugon, Volcano Engine, and other projects have landed in the area.

name: Xuancheng Intelligent Computing Center Construction Project
developer: Xuancheng Economic and Technological Development Zone / Zhejiang Haitao Cloud Data Co. / China Mobile Xuancheng Branch
notes: Xuancheng Data Resources Bureau reports an investment-signing ceremony on March 10, 2025 for the Xuancheng intelligent computing center construction project with the development-zone committee, Zhejiang Haitao Cloud Data, and China Mobile Xuancheng Branch.

name: Xuancheng Integrated Traffic Operations Monitoring and Coordination Command Center Data Center
developer: Xuancheng municipal transport/digital-government authorities
notes: Xuancheng Data Resources Bureau's 2021 digital-Xuancheng summary says the transport monitoring/coordination command center project started in April 2021 and that its data center, field monitoring, physical command center, hardware, and software deployment had been completed.

name: Beijing E-Town 2025 Data Center Whitelist Facilities
developer: 21Vianet / Sinnet / GDS and other Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area operators
notes: Beijing E-Town reports 12 data center projects operated by companies including 21Vianet, Sinnet, and GDS were selected for the 2025 whitelist and may receive compute and green-development support; the citywide 2024-2027 plan focuses on optimizing existing data centers and smart-compute transformation.

name: PDG Greater Beijing Campus (LF1/LF2)
developer: Princeton Digital Group
notes: PDG's China locations page lists a Greater Beijing campus, LF1 and LF2, with 103 MW total capacity across multiple buildings.

name: Beijing Space Data Center System
developer: Beijing Future Space Technology Research Institute and partners
notes: Beijing science commission report says a space data-center plan targets multiple orbital data centers in 700-800 km sun-synchronous orbit, each about 1 GW, with phases in 2025-2027, 2028-2030, and 2031-2035. Included as planned/non-terrestrial compute infrastructure.

name: Tencent Western Cloud Computing Data Center
developer: Tencent Cloud
notes: Chongqing government says Tencent's Chongqing cloud data center in Liangjiang International Cloud Computing Industrial Park covers about 250 mu with RMB 6 billion investment and, when complete, 200,000-server compute/storage capability. People's Daily Chongqing reported phase 2 energization in July 2022.

name: Chongqing Huashao Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Huashao / Dadukou District partners
notes: People's Daily Chongqing reports phase 1 construction began in Dadukou's Jianqiao Park C area; the full plan is about 50,000 8 kW racks, implying roughly 400 MW rack power, with target phase-1 operation in H1 2025. Chongqing data bureau later cites Huashao among the city's large/super-large data centers.

name: Liangjiang International Cloud Computing Industrial Park Data Center Cluster
developer: China Telecom / China Unicom / China Mobile / Chongqing Cable / Liangjiang Cloud / Tencent / Inspur / Tenglong / GDS and others
notes: Chongqing People's Congress/data-bureau material describes Liangjiang International Cloud Computing Industrial Park as the western region's largest concentrated cloud-computing base, planned for 10 large/super-large data centers, with operators including China Telecom, China Unicom, China Mobile, Chongqing Cable, Liangjiang Cloud, Tencent, Inspur, Tenglong, and GDS.

name: China Mobile (Fujian Fuzhou) Data Center
developer: China Mobile Fujian
notes: Changle District reported phase-1 topping out in 2019 on a roughly 185 mu site in Binhai New City. Fuzhou Data Management Bureau later reported more than 9000 total racks, over 13T outbound bandwidth, ISO/ITSS certifications, and selection as a national new data center typical case.

name: Fujian Artificial Intelligence Computing Center / Fuzhou New Area Computing Cluster
developer: Fuzhou New Area / Fujian AI computing-center partners
notes: Fuzhou New Area says Changle District relies on five data centers and has built Fujian's most concentrated compute cluster, with nearly 3000 PFLOPS of intelligent compute; Fuzhou city/provincial planning also identifies Changle as a provincial high-performance data-center cluster location.

name: China Telecom Fuzhou Changle Data Center Building A1
developer: China Telecom Fujian Branch
notes: Uptime Institute award listing identifies China Telecom Fujian Branch as client and Fuzhou Changle Data Center Building A1 as a certified data-center project in Fuzhou.

name: Longyan Artificial Intelligence Computing Power Center Project
developer: Longyan High-tech Zone Economic Development Bureau
notes: Invest Fujian lists a Longyan Xinluo/Gaobei AI computing-power center project with RMB 300 million total investment sought; first phase planned for 100 PFLOPS and a data-labeling team in 2000 sqm of Guanglong Cooperation Industrial Park space plus 800 sqm apartments.

name: Longyan First-batch 50P Artificial Intelligence Computing Center
developer: Longyan city / telecom-operator partners
notes: Longyan Data Management Bureau's 2025 work summary and Fujian DRC reporting say Longyan built its first 50 PFLOPS AI computing center, providing infrastructure for large-scale data computation and AI training.
